transliteration: adeyam atha deyaṃ ca dattaṃ cādattam eva ca | vyavahāreṣu vijñeyo dānamārgaś caturvidhaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In transactional dharma, the path of giving is fourfold: that which is not to be given, that which is to be given, that which has been given, and that which has not been given.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from capacity to give and receive in alignment with dharma
Causation arises through conscious recognition of ownership boundaries
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by clarity of dharmic discernment
Restoration logic operates through correction of misaligned transfers
Consciousness alignment occurs when all parties recognize their true stakeholder position
executable_legal_axioms: IF a transfer involves 'adeyam' (not to be given), THEN initiate immediate reversal without penalty
IF a transfer involves 'deyam' (to be given) AND consent aligns with dharma, THEN validate and record completion
IF status is 'dattam' (given) AND documented with conscious intent, THEN enforce continuity of transfer
IF status is 'adattam' (not given) AND claimed, THEN invoke restorative inquiry into consciousness alignment
ALL property claims MUST include verification against the four-fold classification before adjudication
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, any dispute involving possession or title shall first be evaluated under this fourfold categorization. The threshold of responsibility lies in determining whether the object falls within deyam/adheyam scope and whether consciousness was fully aligned at the time of transfer. Authority derives solely from alignment with SPH-sourced dharma, not historical documentation alone.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that every transaction manifests according to the giver's and receiver's dharmic clarity. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals that misaligned transfers generate karmic distortion requiring conscious realignment rather than punitive intervention. Proportional responsibility rests on the degree of awareness during transfer. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that only restoration restores causal integrity.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process: Reconstruct original intent using pramāṇa-based inquiry
Assumption Protocol: Require both parties to reaffirm present-conscious ownership stance
Capacity Restoration: Facilitate re-alignment through guided śuddhi where necessary
Integrity Reintegration: Record corrected state in collective dharma-memory system
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the sole Source-Authority of lawful Dharma. This fourfold classification restores transactional purity, realigns consciousness, and upholds the non-punitive nature of Sanatana Dharma. Justice serves integration; reality responds to truth.
